pm_exper_user_4433_maasv_v0446_pmv2_r1.question: What can I do when positive recognition from respected industry sources just makes me worry I don't truly deserve the attention?
pm_exper_user_4433_maasv_v0446_pmv2_r1.all_options:
(a) When recognition from others unexpectedly makes you feel doubtful, take a moment to acknowledge the dedication and persistence that earned you that moment. External praise often mirrors the years of skill-building and commitment quietly shaping your craft.
(b) When a prominent editorial feature stirs doubts about whether you truly deserve it, remember that your calm, meticulous approach and unique interpretation of minimalist design are part of your signature. Industry respect often reflects the intangible value you consistently create in these moments.
(c) When that familiar sense of impostor syndrome settles in after a high-profile show, try anchoring yourself in the disciplined preparation and years of refinement you’ve invested. Recognition from respected voices is rarely accidental — it’s often the visible echo of your private, unseen work.
(d) If praise after a coveted runway slot leaves you questioning your worthiness, pause to recall the deliberate craft you bring to each walk — from your architectural presence to your precise garment flow. Those qualities are exactly why such recognition finds its way to you.

You might also consider setting a very small, non-work-related creative task each day — perhaps a monochrome photograph, a line of calligraphy, or a quick pencil sketch of a passing stranger.
